Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap
  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
  SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
  SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
  SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
  SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
  SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
  SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
  SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
  SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
  SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
  SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
  SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
  SPA-N-014: Category separation
  SPA-N-015: Title verification
  SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms

# Project Kestrel — Buyer review of Seller update and disclosure

**Overall recommendation:** Do not accept the Seller’s package as drafted. The general liability regime, broad disclosure and knowledge provisions would materially restrict recourse, while several identified risks remain unresolved at Completion. The positions below are negotiating recommendations; the complete SPA, referenced due-diligence documents and current evidence should be checked before finalising drafting.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price (AUD 4.8m)**. | A higher cap, preferably **100% of price**, with separately negotiated regimes for fundamental warranties, tax and specific indemnities. | **Counter at 100%; negotiate a commercial fallback.** A 20% cap may leave substantial undisclosed business loss with the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; once qualifying claims exceed **AUD 250,000**, only the excess is recoverable. | Lower thresholds and a **tipping basket** under which all qualifying losses are recoverable once the basket is exceeded; aggregate related claims and exclude fundamental, tax, indemnity and fraud claims. | **Reject the excess-only basket and lower the thresholds.** The proposed structure transfers the first AUD 250,000 of qualifying loss to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | General Warranty Claims must be notified within **18 months** after Completion; limitations apply to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | At least **24 months**, preferably sufficient to cover two audit cycles, with separate longer periods for tax and fundamental claims; timely notice should preserve a claim while its amount is assessed. | **Counter at 24 months or longer and separate claim categories.** Some breaches will not become apparent within 18 months. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limit as general warranties. | Separate fundamental warranties, including capacity, authority, ownership, title and freedom from encumbrances, with a **100% price cap**, a substantially longer period and no general thresholds or disclosure qualification. | **Reject the general regime for fundamental warranties.** The Buyer is purchasing all shares and needs effective recourse if ownership or authority is defective. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to **all claims of any nature**. | Expressly preserve claims and remedies for fraud, including fraudulent misrepresentation and fraudulent concealment, notwithstanding caps, thresholds, time limits, disclosure, knowledge, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions. | **Require an express, overriding fraud carve-out.** The proposed blanket language creates unacceptable uncertainty around fraud recourse. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire indexed data room, accounts, statutory registers and public records. | Only matters **fairly and specifically disclosed**, with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope and assess their implications, qualify relevant warranties; identify the final disclosure set and cut-off. | **Reject blanket data-room and public-register disclosure.** Mere availability of a document should not automatically excuse a warranty breach. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to the Buyer or advisers, including matters **discoverable** from the data room or public records. | Delete the qualifier; at most, limit it to actual knowledge of named individuals at signing, without imputed adviser knowledge or a duty to investigate, and preserve fraud and specific indemnities. | **Delete the discoverability standard.** It could defeat claims based on information the Buyer never actually identified or understood. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent condition satisfied on delivery of written consent. No final consent or evidence of associated conditions is included. | A Completion condition requiring valid, unconditional written consent **and satisfaction or waiver of all applicable clause 11.3 conditions**, on terms acceptable to the Buyer, without adverse amendment or payment borne by the Company. | **Make satisfactory consent and related conditions a pre-Completion requirement.** Bluefen represents approximately 30% of FY26 revenue and written consent alone may not complete the contractual requirements. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; release provided after Completion. Facility remains unpaid and no final discharge is included. | Repayment at or before Completion under a binding payoff and funds-flow process, with lender undertakings for release and discharge of all security; reflect the debt-free/cash-free price mechanics and prevent double recovery. | **Require simultaneous repayment and enforceable release arrangements, not a post-Completion promise.** Otherwise the Buyer may acquire the Company with debt and security still outstanding. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | Conditional **AUD 420,000** Completion bonuses are the Seller’s matter but are omitted from the funds flow; applicable on-costs are unknown. | Confirm entitlement and payment timing; include bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs in the funds flow or purchase-price adjustment, funded economically by the Seller, with protection against double counting. | **Quantify and allocate the bonuses and on-costs expressly before Completion.** An unprovided transaction-triggered liability could otherwise reduce the value delivered to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** is recorded as open, but non-payment is not independently verified and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is included. | Verify payment independently and obtain a valid confirmatory assignment or other evidence of ownership; broaden the specific indemnity to resulting IP ownership, usage, infringement, remediation, defence and related losses, without general thresholds or disclosure limitations. | **Obtain evidence and broaden the indemnity.** Payment uncertainty and conditional transfer create exposure beyond the fee itself. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter said not to be expected to be material; access, scope, notification duties and loss remain unestablished. | Complete and document the investigation, preservation, containment and applicable notification assessment; obtain a specific indemnity for incident-related losses and costs, with appropriate control and cooperation provisions. | **Investigate urgently and require tailored protection.** The potential export involves approximately 1,240 records, but access and legal consequences are not yet known. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling **AUD 330,000** characterised as ordinary-course costs; the disclosures do not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. | Review DD-008 and DD-011 together, confirm timing, termination rights and accounting treatment, then allocate any pre-Completion accrual or exceptional commitment through the agreed price mechanics or specific protection. | **Do not accept the ordinary-course characterisation without verification.** Timing and contractual scope determine whether the Buyer is taking an unpriced liability. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | A limitation applies to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise; limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all claims. | A clear hierarchy and separate regimes for general and fundamental warranties, tax covenant, specific indemnities, price adjustments, covenant breaches and fraud; apply each limitation only to expressly identified claim types. | **Rewrite the claims architecture and cross-references.** Otherwise general limitations may unintentionally undermine separately negotiated remedies. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Harbourglass as holder of 100% of issued shares; Seller relies on it for title. | Independently verify the register against constitutional and corporate records, share issuances and transfers, encumbrances and completion deliverables; obtain fundamental title warranties and executed transfers. | **Verify title independently and require clean transfer deliverables.** The register is important evidence but alone does not establish every aspect of title or absence of encumbrances. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties treated as settled under the general regime. | Reopen both: seek a dedicated tax covenant for pre-Completion tax with a longer, appropriately calibrated claim period; obtain comprehensive IP ownership, use, licensing and infringement warranties, plus the Ironquay-specific protection. | **Treat tax and IP as open.** The proposed general cap, time limit and disclosure regime may be inadequate for long-tail tax liabilities and core IP value. |

**Completion priorities:** resolve Bluefen and Riverlark before Completion; verify Ironquay ownership and the bonus allocation; and establish the incident’s status. The Seller’s disclosure that a matter exists is not evidence that the necessary consent, discharge, payment, assignment or investigation has been completed.
